title: Adam Smith and the Invisible Hand
objective: After this level you can explain Smith's idea that self-interest can serve the common good through markets.
summary: Adam Smith argued in 1776 that self-interested trade can serve everyone, as if led by an invisible hand. He also gave government duties and distrusted collusion, and critics say the hand often fails.

cards.headline: Your dinner doesn't depend on the butcher's kindness. Adam Smith said so.
cards.body: In 1776, the Scottish philosopher published The Wealth of Nations. One idea in it became among the most quoted, and most argued over, in all of economics.

cards.headline: The butcher, the brewer and the baker
cards.body: Smith's point was down to earth. You don't get dinner because the butcher, the brewer or the baker feels generous toward you. You get it because selling to you serves their own interest. Nobody has to love you for the bread to show up. Each baker minds his own business, and the town gets fed anyway.

cards.fact: Smith used the phrase 'invisible hand' just once in The Wealth of Nations.
cards.context: In it, a person who "intends only his own gain" is "led by an invisible hand to promote an end which was no part of his intention." The idea: good outcomes for everyone can grow out of many self-interested choices, with no one arranging them. Later writers stretched it, more controversially, into a claim that free markets always deliver the best possible result.

cards.headline: Smith's fine print
cards.body: Smith was no enemy of government. He gave it three duties: defense, justice, and public works like roads and bridges that help society but wouldn't pay a private builder. And he didn't trust business to police itself. People of the same trade, he warned, seldom meet without the talk ending in a conspiracy against the public, or some scheme to raise prices.

cards.headline: The critics
cards.body: Modern critics push further. In 2002, economist Joseph Stiglitz wrote that the invisible hand is invisible, at least in part, because it isn't there. So the question Smith raised stays open: how much good can self-interest do on its own, and where does it need help?

cards.headline: Smith and the invisible hand
learned: Smith published The Wealth of Nations in 1776
Self-interest in trade can feed a whole town
He still gave government three duties
Critics say the invisible hand often fails

questions.prompt: What did Adam Smith's "invisible hand" describe?

options.label: A secret club of merchants fixing prices
options.rationale: Smith warned about such schemes, but that is not the invisible hand.

options.label: Self-interested choices adding up to outcomes that help everyone
A government official steering every trade
options.rationale: The point is that nobody steers.

options.label: A royal stamp that made coins trustworthy
options.rationale: That's Level 4's coin stamp, not Smith's metaphor.

questions.explanation: The invisible hand is Smith's picture of good outcomes arising from many self-interested actions that nobody planned.

questions.prompt: Which statement would Adam Smith himself have agreed with?

options.label: Business owners can always be trusted to serve the public
options.rationale: He warned that traders often scheme to raise prices.

options.label: Government should do nothing at all
Government should provide defense, justice and some public works
A central planner should set every price
options.rationale: Smith argued for trade guided by self-interest, not planning.

questions.explanation: Smith backed markets but gave government three duties: defense, justice and public works like roads and bridges.

questions.prompt: From Level 2: the textbook story that barter came before money goes back to which thinker?

options.label: Karl Marx
options.rationale: The story is older than Marx: it goes back to Smith.

options.label: Milton Friedman
options.rationale: Friedman told Level 6's Yap story, not the barter one.

questions.explanation: Economists since Adam Smith, author of The Wealth of Nations, have told the barter-first story that Level 2 questioned.
